quotes.text: The source database consists of de-identified patient records collected between 2008 and 2019 from routine hospital care.

rationale: The source is named with a time frame (2008-2019, routine hospital care). No dataset name, version or snapshot date, platform, or route from a task to its source record is given, so the score is partial.

quotes.text: Distribution follows a credentialed data use agreement, and the originating institution's IRB approved a consent waiver for this research.
The source database consists of de-identified patient records collected between 2008 and 2019 from routine hospital care.

rationale: Origin (de-identified hospital records), collection setting, data terms (credentialed DUA) and IRB consent waiver are all stated. No repo licence appears in the packet, so no conflict is recorded.

quotes.text: we compared the age, sex and race distribution of the benchmark patients against the U.S. adult inpatient population

rationale: The paper compares patient age, sex and race distributions against a named target population (U.S. adult inpatient population from a national discharge survey). This meets the comparison-against-named-population anchor.

searched: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5. No dedicated unsafe-output test and no bias test on S1-S3. The penalty on unsafe writes is a scoring rule, not a test, and the per-sex/race reporting is only in an S4 code comment, which does not count (G1a).

quotes.text: A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces, and every released task carries a canary string.

rationale: Developer-side controls (held-out split with hidden labels, canary string) are reported. No measured contamination or overlap check is reported; the 99.0% no-leakage clinician check concerns diagnosis disclosure in dialogues, not contamination. Score 1.

quotes.text: Ground truth is isolated from runtime agent access: labels reside in an independent evaluation service disconnected from the agent sandbox with no network route

rationale: Isolation is stated and the mechanism is named (separate evaluation service, no network route from the sandbox, labels not published).

searched: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5. Models are accessed through official APIs with family names only, simulator and judge models are named without snapshot pins, and cases are generated dynamically with no snapshot or software pin reported. Nothing is reported as pinned or frozen.

quotes.text: we ran a scripted reference solution for each task through the grader; all 120 reference solutions were graded correct

rationale: A scripted reference solution was run through the grader for every task and the result (120 of 120 correct) is reported.

quotes.text: Writes are executed against a sandboxed copy of the record, and unnecessary or unsafe writes are penalised in the score.

rationale: Some actions change patient state, so NA does not apply. S1 reports only that unnecessary or unsafe writes are penalised, which is partial detection of side effects. The explicit unchanged-records check appears only in an S4 code comment, which does not count (G1a). Score 1.
searched: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5. No random or trivial agent rate, no chance rate per metric, and no design argument against trivial success is reported.
searched: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5. No do-nothing or random agent result is reported. The no-tools baseline sentence is a language-model baseline, not a trivial agent score.

quotes.text: We validated the grader on 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes, finding a false-accept rate of 1% and a false-reject rate of 2%.

rationale: The benchmark validates its own grader on 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes and reports false-accept and false-reject rates.

quotes.text: Each task was run five times per model with independent random seeds; the temperature was set to 0.7

rationale: The paper states seeds, a temperature of 0.7 and a repeated-run policy (five runs, scores averaged). This is on S1, so the safeguards are not code-only.

quotes.text: test the difference between the two best models with a paired permutation test (p = 0.02)
We report 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for all model scores

rationale: 95% bootstrap CIs are reported for all model scores and a paired permutation test compares the two best models, which covers the headline comparison.

quotes.text: Each task was run five times per model with independent random seeds; the temperature was set to 0.7

contradiction_quotes.text: Each task was run five times per model with independent random seeds

rationale: The paper gives the run count (five), seeds and temperature, and states the runs are independent, so all three elements are present. An S4 code comment says eight runs per task, which conflicts with the reported five. The reported score is kept and the conflict is flagged for verification.

quotes.text: We report 95% confidence intervals computed by bootstrapping over tasks
so the resampling unit is the task; where several tasks share a patient, we resample patients instead to account for clustering

rationale: CIs are reported, the resampling unit (task) is named, and clustering of tasks within patients is handled by resampling patients.

quotes.text: the temperature was set to 0.7
